To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonconvexity of the utility function is an important issue for Internet rate control, and the pricing based algorithm can be developed to address the nonconvex issue and can be made to converge to the optimum.

(1) when users have both concave and nonconcave utility functions, the existing rate control mechanisms can cause instability and network congestion; and (2) a pricing based mechanism can be developed that can be shown to be globally optimal and can avoid instability.

(1) a pricing based algorithm can be developed to solve the dual of a rate allocation problem that can lead to instability when the utility functions of users are sigmoidal; and (2) an algorithm that achieves global optimality can be developed for a rate allocation problem with many users when the utility functions are sigmoidal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the appropriate model for Internet rate allocation?
developing new algorithms and analysis that are more realistic and practical than those in the literature.
the development of a rate control algorithm for Internet applications that can be implemented in a distributed fashion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pricing based mechanism is the best choice for Internet rate control, and that it is possible to design a simple algorithm that converges to the global optimum.
the dual formulation with a pricing based mechanism is a viable approach to rate control with multilevel services and concave as well non-concave utilities.
a distributed rate control mechanism that solves the Lagrangian of the dual formulation of the problem can be designed that is stable, efficient and optimal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the problem of rate control with sigmoidal utility functions is nonconvex, and hence the dual formulation does not necessarily have the desirable properties that the dual formulation for concave utilities has.
we show that the nonconvex nature of the rate control problem needs to be carefully addressed in order to achieve stability and optimality in the Internet.
we develop a rate control algorithm for a realistic setting with both concave and non-concave utility functions, and we show that the algorithm is stable and achieves global optimality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when designing algorithms for rate control, one must be careful in choosing appropriate algorithms for the different types of utility functions.
the problem is inherently nonconvex and hence the standard approach based on convexity does not apply.
the dual formulation is more robust than the primal formulation and can be used to develop rate allocation algorithms that are more stable and more efficient than those based on primal formulations.
